When the user asks you to build, run, or verify something, the deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output — not a description of one. You MUST use your tools to take action — do not describe what you would do or plan to do without actually doing it. arguments.title: October Quarterly All-Hands — Agenda Template
arguments.body:
# October Quarterly All-Hands — Agenda Template

**Date:** October [date, year]  
**Time:** [start–end, time zone]  
**Facilitator:** [name]  
**Note-taker / question coordinator:** HR  
**Attendees:** [team / invite list]

## Purpose
Share a concise company update, cover approved current topics, and answer useful questions submitted in advance.

## Agenda

| Time | Segment | Lead | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0:00–0:05] | Welcome, purpose, and format | [Facilitator] | Remind attendees that questions were collected in advance; this is structured Q&A, not open-ended live Q&A. |
| [0:05–0:15] | Short company update | [Presenter] | Keep to current, approved company context. |
| [0:15–0:35] | Current-quarter priorities and key work | [Topic owners] | Cover approved current topics; note relevant decisions, progress, and boundaries. |
| [0:35–0:50] | Collected-question Q&A | [Facilitator + topic owners] | HR groups questions in advance. Answer live only when the question concerns an approved current topic and is useful to the whole company. |
| [0:50–0:57] | Follow-ups and owner callouts | [Facilitator / named owners] | Identify questions to answer asynchronously or route to a named owner, with an owner and expected follow-up channel/date where known. |
| [0:57–1:00] | Close | [Facilitator] | Recap follow-ups and where to send additional questions after the meeting. |

## Questions and follow-ups
- HR collects and organizes questions before the meeting, grouping duplicates and prioritizing questions useful to the whole company.
